title: Dimension balance for the geometrically regular p-root comparison
statement: Let k be a field of prime characteristic p, A a Noetherian local k-algebra [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] geometrically regular over k [def-weil-pbc-g-ring], and a : Fin n → k such that (d a_i) is k-linearly independent in Omega[k/F_p] [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. Give A its composite F_p-algebra structure through k. Let B = A[X_i]/(X_i^p-algebraMap(a_i)) be the actual p-root quotient [lem-weil-pbc-pth-root-algebra-local]. For every local instance on B making A → B local, put L = B/m_B and beta = Algebra.residueDifferentialComparison p A B [lem-weil-pbc-pth-root-residue-differentials]. Then finrank_L(ker beta) = finrank_L(coker beta). The whole absolute differential modules need not be finite dimensional.

proof.text: Use the trivial finite purely inseparable extension to obtain regularity of A and identify its conormal dimension d; the universe lift of k and tensor left-unit equivalence implement the trivial extension. The family is already indexed by Fin n, and this argument includes n=0.

*The extension $k'$.* By [lem-weil-pbc-pth-roots-extension-degree] the subfield $k(a_1^{1/p},\dots,a_n^{1/p})$ of an algebraic closure of $k$ has degree $p^n$. Let $k'=k[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(x_1^p-a_1,\dots,x_n^p-a_n)$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Using $x_j^p=a_j$, $k'$ is spanned over $k$ by the $p^n$ monomials $x^e$, $0\le e_j<p$, so $\dim_kk'\le p^n$; the $k$-algebra map $k'\to k(a_1^{1/p},\dots,a_n^{1/p})$, $x_j\mapsto a_j^{1/p}$, is surjective (its image $k[a_1^{1/p},\dots,a_n^{1/p}]$ is a field, being a domain finite over $k$ [lem-weil-pbc-finite-dimensional-domain-is-field], and contains the generators). Comparing dimensions it is an isomorphism: $k'$ is a field with $[k':k]=p^n$. For $y=\sum_e\lambda_ex^e\in k'$, $y^p=\sum_e\lambda_e^pa^e\in k$ ($p$-th power is additive in characteristic $p$), so $k'/k$ is finite purely inseparable [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension].

*The ring $A'$ and its dimension.* Put $A'=A\otimes_kk'\cong A[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(x_1^p-a_1,\dots,x_n^p-a_n)$ (tensoring the presentation of step 2 with $A$). By [lem-weil-pbc-purely-inseparable-base-change-local-ring]: $A\to A'$ is finite and free, $A'$ is a Noetherian local ring whose maximal ideal $\mathfrak m'$ is the only prime containing $\mathfrak mA'$, and $K'=A'/\mathfrak m'$ is a finite extension of $K$, with $A'/\mathfrak mA'\cong K\otimes_kk'$ finite dimensional over $K$. By geometric regularity [def-weil-pbc-g-ring] ($k'/k$ finite purely inseparable, step 2) $A'$ is regular, hence a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme]. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-height-formula] for the flat map $A\to A'$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] and $\mathfrak m'$ over $\mathfrak m$, $\dim A'=\dim A+\dim A'/\mathfrak mA'$; every prime of the finite-dimensional $K$-algebra $A'/\mathfrak mA'$ is maximal (a domain finite over $K$ is a field [lem-weil-pbc-finite-dimensional-domain-is-field]), so $\dim A'/\mathfrak mA'=0$ and $\dim A'=d$. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-cotangent-dimension] $\dim_{K'}\mathfrak m'/\mathfrak m'^2=d$.

Use [lem-weil-pbc-pth-root-residue-differentials] for the beta defined in the statement. Its kernel is finitely generated and its cokernel has dimension n. The local instance in that theorem agrees with the given instance by proof irrelevance.

*The conormal rows.* Let $(B,\mathfrak n,L)$ be a local $\mathbf F_p$-algebra; we apply this to $(A,\mathfrak m,K)$ and $(A',\mathfrak m',K')$. The Jacobi-Zariski sequence of $\mathbf F_p\to B\to L$ [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-homology-sequence] is exact: $H_1(L_{L/\mathbf F_p})\to H_1(L_{L/B})\xrightarrow{\partial_B}L\otimes_B\Omega_{B/\mathbf F_p}\xrightarrow{w}\Omega_{L/\mathbf F_p}\to\Omega_{L/B}\to0$. Here $H_1(L_{L/\mathbf F_p})=0$ [lem-weil-pbc-field-char-p-h1-cotangent-vanishing], $\Omega_{L/B}=0$ and $\theta:H_1(L_{L/B})\cong\mathfrak n/\mathfrak n^2$ [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-surjection-h1], and $\partial_B=\delta\circ\theta$ with $\delta(f)=1\otimes\mathrm df$ (the case $S=B$ of [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-connecting-map-naturality]; there $\iota$ is the identity by [lem-weil-pbc-nl-presentation-h1-functoriality] (2)). Hence $0\to\mathfrak n/\mathfrak n^2\xrightarrow{\delta}L\otimes_B\Omega_{B/\mathbf F_p}\xrightarrow{w}\Omega_{L/\mathbf F_p}\to0$ is exact. For $B=A$ tensor this sequence of $K$-vector spaces with $K'$ over $K$ (exact, as $K'$ is a free $K$-module): $0\to\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2\otimes_KK'\to K'\otimes_A\Omega_{A/\mathbf F_p}\to K'\otimes_K\Omega_{K/\mathbf F_p}\to0$ is exact.

*The map $\gamma$.* Let $\gamma:K'\otimes_K\Omega_{K/\mathbf F_p}\to\Omega_{K'/\mathbf F_p}$, $x\otimes\mathrm db\mapsto x\,\mathrm db$. The Jacobi-Zariski sequence of $\mathbf F_p\to K\to K'$ [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-homology-sequence], $H_1(L_{K'/\mathbf F_p})\to H_1(L_{K'/K})\xrightarrow{\partial}K'\otimes_K\Omega_{K/\mathbf F_p}\xrightarrow{\gamma}\Omega_{K'/\mathbf F_p}\to\Omega_{K'/K}\to0$, is exact and $H_1(L_{K'/\mathbf F_p})=0$ [lem-weil-pbc-field-char-p-h1-cotangent-vanishing]; so $\ker\gamma\cong H_1(L_{K'/K})$ and $\operatorname{coker}\gamma\cong\Omega_{K'/K}$. Since $K'/K$ is finite (step 3, [lem-weil-pbc-purely-inseparable-base-change-local-ring]), [lem-weil-pbc-cartier-equality] gives $\dim_{K'}\Omega_{K'/K}=\dim_{K'}H_1(L_{K'/K})<\infty$. So $\ker\gamma$ and $\operatorname{coker}\gamma$ have the same finite dimension.

*Snake lemma.* Consider the commutative diagram of $K'$-vector spaces with exact rows $0\to\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2\otimes_KK'\to K'\otimes_A\Omega_{A/\mathbf F_p}\to K'\otimes_K\Omega_{K/\mathbf F_p}\to0$ and $0\to\mathfrak m'/\mathfrak m'^2\to K'\otimes_{A'}\Omega_{A'/\mathbf F_p}\to\Omega_{K'/\mathbf F_p}\to0$ (step 5) and vertical maps $\alpha$ (induced by $A\to A'$, which maps $\mathfrak m$ into $\mathfrak m'$), $\beta$ (step 4), $\gamma$ (step 6). The squares commute because $\Omega_{A/\mathbf F_p}\to\Omega_{A'/\mathbf F_p}$, $\mathrm db\mapsto\mathrm d(b\otimes1)$, is compatible with $\mathrm d$ and with the residue maps [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]: $\beta(1\otimes\mathrm df)=1\otimes\mathrm d(f\otimes1)=\delta'(\alpha(f))$ for $f\in\mathfrak m$, and $\gamma(1\otimes\mathrm d\bar b)=\mathrm d\bar b=w'(\beta(1\otimes\mathrm db))$ for $b\in A$. The snake lemma [lem-weil-pbc-snake-lemma-modules] gives an exact sequence $0\to\ker\alpha\to\ker\beta\to\ker\gamma\to\operatorname{coker}\alpha\to\operatorname{coker}\beta\to\operatorname{coker}\gamma\to0$ of finite-dimensional $K'$-vector spaces: $\alpha$ goes between spaces of the same dimension $d$ (steps 1, 3), so $\dim\ker\alpha=\dim\operatorname{coker}\alpha$; $\dim\ker\gamma=\dim\operatorname{coker}\gamma<\infty$ (step 6); $\dim\ker\beta\le n$, $\dim\operatorname{coker}\beta=n$ (step 4). The alternating sum of dimensions in a finite exact sequence of finite-dimensional vector spaces is $0$, so $\dim\ker\beta-\dim\operatorname{coker}\beta=(\dim\ker\alpha-\dim\operatorname{coker}\alpha)+(\dim\ker\gamma-\dim\operatorname{coker}\gamma)=0$, hence the kernel and cokernel dimensions of beta agree.

lean.statement:
theorem pthRoot_residue_dimension_balance
    (k : Type u) (A : Type v) [Field k] [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    [IsLocalRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] [CharP k p]
    (hA : IsGeometricallyRegular k A) (n : ℕ) (a : Fin n → k) :
    letI := ZMod.algebra k p
    letI := ((algebraMap k A).comp (algebraMap (ZMod p) k)).toAlgebra
    let B := pthRootAlgebra p n A (fun i ↦ algebraMap k A (a i))
    ∀ [IsLocalRing B] [IsLocalHom (algebraMap A B)],
    LinearIndependent k (fun i ↦ KaehlerDifferential.D (ZMod p) k (a i)) →
    let L := IsLocalRing.ResidueField B
    let β := residueDifferentialComparison p A B
    Module.finrank L β.ker =
      Module.finrank L ((L ⊗[B] KaehlerDifferential (ZMod p) B) ⧸ β.range)
